Note::to_nfd¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::to_nfd() const

Decompose Every Cell To Unicode Normalization Form D¶

to_nfd() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell converted to NFD — the canonical decomposed form. Every precomposed accented character is split into its base letter followed by its combining marks: the single code point é (U+00E9) becomes e + U+0301 (combining acute).

NFD is the useful form when you want to operate on the marks — for example strip_accents only removes standalone combining marks and the common Latin-1 precomposed letters, so to_nfd().strip_accents() folds a much wider range of accented text to ASCII. It does not change how the text renders, only its bytes; pair it with lengths_chars to see the change.

to_nfd is shape-preserving, cell-independent, idempotent, and returns a fresh Note. Requires the Unicode backend.

Example 1: A Precomposed Accent Is Split¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"café", "abc"}).to_nfd();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["café", "abc"]

The render is unchanged.

Example 2: The Character Count Shows The Change¶

const auto out = pluss::make_note({"café", "abc"}).to_nfd();
const auto bytes = out.lengths_bytes();
const auto chars = out.lengths_chars();
std::cout << "bytes=[" << bytes[0] << ", " << bytes[1] << "] chars=["
          << chars[0] << ", " << chars[1] << "]\n";

Output¶

bytes=[6, 3] chars=[5, 3]

"café" is now 5 code points (c a f e ◌́) in 6 bytes; the ASCII cell is untouched.

  • Note::to_nfc: the opposite direction — canonical composition.
